faqs.q: What is the SI unit of density?
faqs.a: Kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m³). Water at 4 °C is 1,000 kg/m³, which is also 1 g/cm³ and 1 g/mL.

faqs.q: How do g/cm³ and kg/m³ relate?
faqs.a: 1 g/cm³ = 1,000 kg/m³ exactly. The two scales differ by a factor of one thousand.

faqs.q: What is the density of air?
faqs.a: About 1.225 kg/m³ at sea level and 15 °C — try converting that to lb/ft³ (≈ 0.0765).
